```{r}
# Part Two Question 1
library(tidyverse) # loads packages
library(rvest)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
communityareas<-read_html("https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community_areas_of_Chicago") # loads the html file


#EXTRACT TABLE AS DATAFRAME
CAtable <- communityareas %>%
  html_element("table") %>%
  html_table()

head(CAtable)

FinalCAtable<- CAtable[-c(1,79),] %>% # removes rows 1 & 79 from original
  select(No.,Name,Population) %>% # only keeps the number name and population
  mutate(
    Population = str_remove_all(Population,","),
    Population = as.numeric(Population) # removes comma and makes population numeric
)

FinalCAtable %>% slice(24) # West Town

FinalCAtable %>%  # Arranges population high to low then gets top 5
  arrange(desc(Population)) %>%
  head(5)

```

```{r, part 1 question2}
library(readr)
bookhtml <- read_html("https://books.toscrape.com/")


eachbook <- bookhtml |> # each book section
  html_elements("article.product_pod")
eachbook

title = eachbook |> #title of each book
  html_element("h3") |> 
  html_text2()
title


price = eachbook |> #price of each book
  html_element("p.price_color") |> 
  html_text2()
price


availability = eachbook |>  #availility of each book
  html_element("p.instock.availability") |> 
  html_text2()
availability

bookstoscrape <- tibble( # creates table
  title, 
  price,
  availability
)



cleanbookstoscrape <-bookstoscrape %>% # cleans table and makes price numeric
   mutate(
    price = str_remove_all(price,"£"),
    price = as.numeric(price)
)

write_csv(cleanbookstoscrape, "books.csv") # saves table as csv and in repo

```

```{r part 3}
library(httr)
library(jsonlite)

# answer to part 3 question 1
url <- "https://data.cityofchicago.org/resource/v6vf-nfxy.json"

params <- list( #creates a filter that will go through API
  community_area = "24",
   `$where` = "created_date >= '2026-01-01T00:00:00'",
  `$order` = "created_date DESC",
  `$limit` = 1000
)
res <- GET(url, query = params)

#question 2
dat <- fromJSON(content(res, "text")) # dataframe created fromJSON 
head(dat)

nrow(dat) #number of rows

colnames(dat) #column names


dat %>% 
  count(sr_type, sort = TRUE)%>% # uses data frame and sorts by sr type from descending order then gives top 10. Answer to 3
  head(10)

```


• Gross Rent as a Percentage of Household Income, “Total”: B25070_001E • Gross Rent as a Percentage of Household Income, "50.0 percent or more":B25070_010E • Median Household Income: B19013_001E

```{r}

# step 2 creates dataset for Ohio with all 3 variables for all Ohio counties
Ohioincome <- get_acs(geography = "tract", 
                   variables = c(
                     percent_rent_total = "B25070_001", # gets all 3 variables
                     fiftypercent_rent="B25070_010",
                       median_householdinc= "B19013_001" ),
                   state = "OH", , 
                   year = 2024, 
                   survey = "acs5") 
head(Ohioincome) 
```
```{r}
library(tidyr)
library(janitor)

# step 3
wideOhioIncome <-Ohioincome  %>% #uses Ohioincome dataset and gets rid of moe
  select(-moe)%>%
separate_wider_delim( #used AI here to figure out how to seperate the name into different columns
    cols = NAME,
    delim = "; ",
    names = c("census_tract", "county", "state")
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider( #makes it wider by giving each variable its own column
    id_cols = c(GEOID,census_tract,county,state),
    names_from = variable,
    values_from = c(estimate),
  ) %>%
  clean_names() %>%
#step 3.2
  mutate( # adds  variable to table
    severe_burden_rate = fiftypercent_rent/ percent_rent_total
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(severe_burden_rate))
print(wideOhioIncome)

```
STEP Four
```{r}
#gets median and mode for severe burden rate
wideOhioIncome %>%
  summarise(
    mean_inc   = mean(severe_burden_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_inc = median(severe_burden_rate, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

#2
countyrates <- wideOhioIncome %>% #groups by county gets mean and arranges them
  group_by(county) %>%
  summarise(avg_rate = mean(severe_burden_rate, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(avg_rate))

#top 5 highest rates
head(countyrates, 5)

#top 5 lowest rates
tail(countyrates, 5)
```
Step 5

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

#creates scatterplot
ggplot(data = wideOhioIncome, aes(x = median_householdinc, y = severe_burden_rate)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, color = "blue") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "red", se = FALSE) +
  
  labs(
    title = "Median Household Income vs. Severe Burden Rate",
    subtitle = "Ohio Census Tracts",
    x = "Median Household Income ($)",
    y = "Severe Burden Rate"
  ) +

  theme_minimal()


#creates bar graph

top_5 <- head(countyrates, 5)
low_5 <- tail(countyrates, 5)

#getting them to be percentages 
countybargraph <- bind_rows(top_5, low_5) %>%
  mutate(avg_ratepercent = avg_rate * 100)


ggplot(countybargraph, aes(x = avg_ratepercent, y = reorder(county, avg_ratepercent))) + # orders from hight to low
  geom_col( fill = "blue") +
  labs(
    title = "Top 5 and Bottom 5 Counties by Severe Housing Burden Rate",
    subtitle = "Ohio Counties",
    x = "Average Severe Housing Burden Rate (%)",
    y = "County"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
